title: CEO Interview with Tobias Pohl of CELUS
gist: Interview with CELUS CEO Tobias Pohl: the Munich startup automates the early phase of electronics (board) design, going from functional requirements to a first schematic and BoM, with every recommendation traced to a cited digital datasheet (CUBO). Used by 70,000+ engineers, it positions traceability against both incumbent EDA vendors adding AI and ungrounded general-purpose LLMs, and is moving toward full agentic design flows via MCP.

insights.claim: CELUS, a Munich-based company founded in 2018, runs an AI-powered electronics design platform used by more than 70,000 engineers.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Indicates meaningful bottom-up adoption for an AI hardware-design startup.
insights.locator: Tobias Pohl is co-founder and CEO of CELUS

insights.claim: CELUS's platform takes an engineer from functional requirements to a first schematic and bill of materials, via a Design Assistant where the engineer describes a board, approves a plan and reviews the output.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: AI is moving upstream into requirements-to-schematic, a front-end segment of PCB/electronics design that incumbents under-serve.

insights.claim: The early phase of electronics design is slow and mostly manual: engineers read dozens of datasheets, draw connections by hand, and can discover weeks later that a component is near end of life or incompatible.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Late discovery of EOL/incompatible parts drives schedule risk, which is the pain point AI front-end tools monetize.

insights.claim: CELUS's strongest usage verticals are IoT, automotive and industrial applications.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Shows where AI-assisted board design is gaining traction first.
insights.locator: What application areas are your strongest?

insights.claim: CELUS differentiates by tracing each recommendation to a cited CUBO (a digital datasheet with schematics, BoMs and footprints), whereas general-purpose language models describe circuits convincingly but have no grounding in manufacturer data.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Grounded, citation-backed AI may beat generic LLMs in liability-heavy engineering domains.
insights.quote: General-purpose language models can describe a circuit convincingly but have no grounding in manufacturer data.
insights.locator: What does the competitive landscape look like

insights.claim: Because the engineer who signs off on a design owns every error, buyers of AI design tools demand provenance for each decision before accepting it.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Explainability/provenance is a buying criterion for AI engineering tools, not a nice-to-have.
insights.quote: An engineer who signs off on a design owns every error in it
insights.locator: What keeps your customers up at night?

insights.claim: Established EDA vendors have mature schematic tools and are adding AI features on top, while CELUS shows its plan to the engineer for approval before building and self-checks its output with presented evidence.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Incumbents bolt on AI; startups compete on AI-native workflow with human approval gates.
insights.locator: What does the competitive landscape look like

insights.claim: CELUS is building a full agentic design flow, connecting many tools via MCP, and expanding CELUS CAD to cover a broader segment of the workflow.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: MCP is becoming the integration fabric for agentic EDA tooling.
insights.locator: What new features/technology are you working on?

insights.claim: CELUS integrates with incumbent tools such as Siemens EDA and distributes through partner platforms like the NXP Block Diagram Designer powered by CELUS, while also working directly with suppliers and distributor shopping carts.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Partnership-led distribution with chip vendors and EDA incumbents rather than head-on competition.
insights.locator: How do customers normally engage with your company?

insights.claim: CELUS uses a freemium model: engineers can sign up free on Celus.io, with more advanced solutions sold to enterprises and professionals.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Bottom-up PLG motion explains the large user count; monetization depends on enterprise conversion.
insights.locator: How do customers normally engage with your company?
